messages:
juan (customer): Hey team — running a nightly job to embed ~500k docs and we're seeing a ton of 429s. Started around 03:10 UTC. No other errors, just 429 rate_limit. Example: 'HTTP 429: Rate limit exceeded'.

alexa (support): Sorry you're hitting that, juan. Do you have a minimal repro and the request pattern (batch size, concurrency)? Also, can you share the response headers from one 429 (x-rate-limit-*, retry-after)?

juan (customer): Repro is simple: we POST batches of 1024 texts to /v1/embeddings concurrently with 20 workers. Payload size ~ 8MB per request. We saw a few headers: `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 15` and `retry-after: 30` in some responses.

alexa (support): Thanks. Two quick thoughts: 1) embedding endpoints have both per-project per-minute tokens and concurrent request limits — large batches + 20 workers can trip burst windows. 2) Are you using retries with backoff and jitter?

juan (customer): We use a naive retry: sleep 5s then retry (no jitter). Tried lowering concurrency to 5 and that reduced 429s but job time went way up. Want to avoid rewriting our job if possible.

sam (eng-sre): @alexa ping — can we get request IDs from juan so we can correlate on infra side? Also what model are they hitting? Different model variants have different embeddings throughput and concurrent limits.

juan (customer): Model is "redwood-embed-1024" (the new default). Request IDs: `req_01E9X3A4`, `req_01E9X3B7` (from response body).

alexa (support): Good. Sam, I'm attaching the logs from juan's responses below for quick triage.

--- pasted response snippet ---
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 04 Jun 2025 03:14:05 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 30
X-Rate-Limit-Limit: 1200
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0
X-Rate-Limit-Reset: 25
{
  "error": {"message": "Rate limit exceeded", "type": "rate_limit"},
  "request_id": "req_01E9X3A4"
}
--- end snippet ---

sam (eng-sre): Thanks. Limit 1200/s (or per-minute window?) Looks like the header is per-minute token window here (1200 units) and your batches consume lots of embedding units per request because of # of inputs and model dimensionality. Two paths: (A) client side: reduce batch size to ~128 and add exponential backoff with jitter. (B) infra/product: check if this tenant is on default quotas and whether a quota bump/dedicated pool is warranted for large nightly jobs.

juan (customer): Curious — is there a way to keep batch size high for throughput but not hit the burst limit? We want to use large batches to reduce total tokens per-request overhead.

alexa (support): One pattern that helps is staggered batching: keep large batch sizes but serialize start times across workers and limit concurrent inflight requests (e.g., concurrency=4) so you get large payloads but avoid high parallelism. Also enable client-side prefix caching if you have repeated prefixes.

sam (eng-sre): Adding to that: implement token accounting per request and check returned `X-Rate-Limit-Remaining`. If it's low, throttle proactively instead of waiting for 429. Also use exponential backoff with random jitter — sample pseudocode: `backoff = min(cap, base * 2^retries) * (0.8 + rand() * 0.4)`.

juan (customer): Understood. Can you reproduce from infra side so we can confirm it's quota and not a bug? I can schedule a quick run (with smaller sample) if you want.

sam (eng-sre): Yes please. Please run a short job: 2000 docs, batch_size=1024, concurrency=8, model=redwood-embed-1024, start at 04:00 UTC and include the response headers and request_id for any 429s. We'll instrument the serving nodes and check quota accounting and per-node shedding behavior.

juan (customer): Scheduled and will run at 04:00. Attaching our sample cURL to reproduce: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1024","input":["doc1","doc2",...]}'
```

juan (customer): Also noticed occasional dimension mismatch errors in past runs: some vectors were length 512 not 1024. Could that be related?

alexa (support): Dimension mismatch is concerning — that indicates a model variant fallback or a different model was routed. Sam, can routing fallback to a smaller-dim variant when capacity constrained? If so, that could explain the dimension difference.

sam (eng-sre): We do have fallback policies to lower-capacity model variants under overload for some tenants, but we should not change dimensionality for embedding contracts — that would be a regression. I'll check the rollout rules and recent routing logs for juan's project.

sam (eng-sre): Quick initial findings: juan's project is on the default shared pool. We saw several concurrent request spikes from the job that matched the 429 window around 03:14 UTC. No evidence the runtime forcibly returned different-dimension embeddings in that window, but I see two requests later that hit a different model instance (req_01E9X7D2) which returned vectors length 512 — that's on us to investigate further.

alexa (support): For immediate mitigation we recommend: 1) reduce concurrency to 4 and keep batch_size=512; 2) add jittered exponential backoff; 3) if nightly SLA requires faster throughput, open a ticket to request a temporary quota bump or consider Dedicated capacity.

juan (customer): I'll try concurrency=4 + backoff tonight. Also we want help opening a quota bump request — ping me what info you need.

alexa (support): We'll open an internal ticket. Please DM me your project ID and peak qps requirements (per-minute embedding units). We'll escalate to capacity planning.

juan (customer): Project ID: proj_0xC12. Peak planned throughput: 10M embeddings per night (~3000 reqs/min at current batch size).

sam (eng-sre): Noted. We'll correlate with infra logs and follow up in this thread once we confirm whether the 512-dim responses were a routing bug or a client mixup. Thanks for the repro run, juan.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2025-06-04T02:45:00 UTC completed: routing-service v3.14.7

alexa (support): FYI deploy just finished ~25m before the incident window — we'll include that in the investigation.

juan (customer): The scheduled run completed — still saw ~8% 429s at concurrency=8, batch=1024. At concurrency=4 + batch=512 it's much cleaner (~0.4% 429). Will send headers/req_ids in DM.

sam (eng-sre): Received the DM. Initial conclusion: quota exhaustion + transient routing quiescence during deploy. We'll follow up with a proposed quota change and a short-term soft-rate-limit exemption for proj_0xC12 while capacity is provisioned.

alexa (support): Closing loop: juan, we'll keep this thread updated with the ticket number and timeline. Meanwhile please implement the client-side backoff + reduce concurrency to 4 for tonight's run. Thanks everyone.

juan (customer): Thanks all :thumbsup:
